items.hook: Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, previously called the Swift Gamma-Ray Burst Explorer, is a NASA three-instrument space observatory for studying gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) and monitoring the afterglow in X-ray and UV/visible light at the location of a burst.
items.body: It was launched on 20 November 2004, aboard a Delta II launch vehicle. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: Shingles vaccine may lower risk of stroke and heart failure
items.body: Being vaccinated against shingles has been linked to a lower risk of cardiovascular disease before, but now a study suggests that the vaccine that is currently being used reduces the odds more than earlier versions of the shot

items.hook: Workout patch delivers some of the benefits of exercise with no exertion
items.body: Injecting muscle cells beneath the skin of mice led to a patch of self-contracting cells that boosted their muscle mass, bone density and even markers of good brain, immune and liver function

items.hook: Peter [de] Thellusson was a Genevan businessman and banker who settled in London, and became a British subject in 1762.
items.body: He amassed a fortune through commerce and, when he died in 1797, he owned more than 4,000 acres of land in England. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: The Priest Barracks of Dachau Concentration incarcerated clergy who had opposed the Nazi regime of Adolf Hitler.
items.body: From December 1940, Berlin ordered the transfer of clerical prisoners held at other camps, and Dachau became the centre for imprisonment of clergymen. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.
